risk_if_not_implemented: Without Establish Redundancy for Vital Security, Compliance & Resilience Staff, data, software and system images cannot be reliably restored within required recovery objectives following a disruption. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Concentration / Single-Point Dependency Failure (R-OR-2), Loss of Critical Knowledge / Capability (R-PE-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Assigned Security, Compliance & Resilience Responsibilities
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to assign one or more qualified individuals with the mission and resources to centrally-manage, coordinate, develop, implement and maintain an enterprise-wide Security, Compliance & Resilience Program (SCRP).
compensating_control_1.justification: Assigned Security, Compliance & Resilience Responsibilities (GOV-05) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Establish Redundancy for Vital Security, Compliance & Resilience Staff (HRS-16.3) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Identify Critical Skills & Gaps
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to evaluate the critical security, compliance and resilience skills needed to support the organization's mission and identify gaps that exist.
compensating_control_2.justification: Identify Critical Skills & Gaps (HRS-16) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Establish Redundancy for Vital Security, Compliance & Resilience Staff (HRS-16.3) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
